about: Grammar the tutor added on her Tutor page: her words, Claude's rewrite as a rule with a letter-number, and her answer. Only her 'Yes, add it' adds the rule (scripts/tutor_grammar.py).

items.text: add to the grammar rule that is about collocations the updated list of all verb-prepositions collocations. you can find the list on the doc or in the flash card sets (named all ver collocations)

versions.why: This is an instruction to update an existing collocations rule with a list from another document, not a new grammar rule, and it has no rule content or examples to turn into a card.

items.text:
using mufaddal. 
mufaddal (favorite) in Arabic varries. 
we treat it as an adjective that follows its noun with definiteness and gender. 
and because pronoun-ending nouns are considered definitive, we follow such nouns with el + mufaddal/e/a 
akli el-mufaddal = my favorite food.
makano el-mufaddal = his favorite place.
awaa3iha el-mufaddaleen = her favorite clothes. 

mufaddal + 3ind. 
sometimes, when favorite is put alone in a sentence with no noun, or the noun proceeds it, we use 3ind to support it. 

this is my favorite = had/i el-mufaddal 3indi 

we can also use 3ind anytime, not necessarily to support mufaddal when it's alone. 
hadi el-buza el-mufaddala 3indo = this is his favorite ice cream 
so t becomes a preference thing.

versions.name: mufaddal + 3ind
versions.one_line: Mufaddal (favorite) is an adjective that follows its noun and matches it in gender and definiteness; a noun with a pronoun ending counts as definite, so it takes el-mufaddal, and 3ind + the person can support it when it stands alone or after the noun.

examples.english: this is his favorite ice cream

versions.why: English puts 'favorite' before the noun and never changes it, but in Arabic mufaddal comes after the noun and has to agree with it, and 3ind makes it a matter of preference.

overlaps.name: noun + adjective
overlaps.why: Mufaddal is an adjective that goes after its noun, and el- placement and gender follow the same noun + adjective pattern.

items.text:
a8lab + nafs
both a8lab nafs take a el + noun to mean most and same. 
nafs = same. 
nafs + el + noun = the same...
nafs el-tari2 = the same road. 
possessive/pronoun-ending nouns are also definitive. so nafs shanteti = same as my bag 

to say the same, we say nafs el-ishi. 

a8lab = most/ most of 
a8lab + el + noun = most / most of... 
 
a8lab el-naas = most people 
a8lab akli = most of my food. 
a8lab awaa3i sitti = most of my grandmother's clothes.

nafs loan juzdani = the same color as my purse/wallet

versions.name: a8lab and nafs + definite noun
versions.one_line: a8lab (most of) and nafs (the same) are followed by a definite noun, meaning el- + noun or a noun with a possessive ending.
versions.formula: a8lab / nafs + el- + noun (or noun + possessive ending)
versions.why: English says 'most people' and 'the same road' with no marker on the noun, but here the noun after a8lab or nafs must be definite, and a noun with a possessive ending already counts as definite.

overlaps.name: nafs + el-: the same
overlaps.why: A17 also covers nafs + el- + noun = the same, so a learner could mix up the two cards, while a8lab follows the same pattern with a different meaning.

items.text:
taani and 8eir 
Taani has two particularly useful functions: identifying something as second in a sequence and referring to something additional or different.
Rule 1: Taani + noun = Second / the second…
When taani comes before a noun, it can identify the second item or stage in a sequence.
Structure: taani + noun
Meaning: Second / the second…
Rule 2: El- + noun + el-taani / el-taaniye = The second / the other…
When el-taani or el-taaniye comes after the noun, it identifies a particular item as second or distinguishes it from another item.
Structure: el- + noun + el-taani / el-taaniye
Meaning: The second… / the other…
Rule 3: Noun + taani / taaniye = Another / a different…
When taani follows the noun without el-, it can mean another or a different one, rather than specifically the second item in a sequence.
Structure: noun + taani / taaniye
Meaning: Another… / a different…
Remember: The difference between second and another often depends on word order and context.
 
4. 8eir (غير): Different / Other
8eir is used to express difference or alternatives. Its interpretation depends on the phrase and context.
Rule 1: 8eir + noun = A different… / other…
When 8eir comes before a noun, it can introduce something different or other than what was previously mentioned.
Structure: 8eir + noun
Meaning: A different… / other…
8eir / mu5talef also takes the preposition (3an) when we want to say other than / different from. 
8eir can be used as an adjective as well and be put after the noun with "el" but it's rarely used and it's preferable to use it a function word. 
mu5talef is also different, but it's different from 8eir
• M5talef (مختلف) = different in nature or characteristics.
• 8eir (غير) = other than / another / something else.
They can overlap in meaning, but they are not interchangeable in every sentence.
items.example: taani 7ada = second person / the second person yoami el-tani = my second day, 8eir bluze = another/different shirt, ishi taani = something else, huwwe 8eir 3anni = he is different than me.

versions.name: taani and 8eir
versions.one_line: taani before a noun means second; after the noun without el- it means another; 8eir before a noun means a different or other one, and 8eir + 3an means different from.
versions.formula: taani + noun = second | el- + noun + el-taani = the second / the other | noun + taani = another | 8eir + noun = different / other
versions.why: English uses different words for second, another and different, but Arabic uses the same words, so the meaning depends on word order and context.

overlaps.name: taani: before or after the noun
overlaps.why: A14 also covers taani before or after the noun, with and without el-.

items.text:
Awal and aa5er uses 
in spoken Arabic, function words mean different things depending on where they're put in a sentence, whether they're followed by an "el" or not, or if an overruling grammar is present in the sentence. 
Awal can mean First / the first or the beginning of 
Awal + noun (without el) is first or the first. 
Awal + el + noun = the beginning of... 
a pronoun/possessive-ending noun is also considered a definitive noun: so awal yoami = the beginning of my day. 
to work around this rule, and because idafa always surpasses/overrules other grammar rules, we use ili or the adjective form of awal: awal (M) and oola (f) 
so my first day = yoami el-awal / awal yoam ili. 
to say first yyou can also use the adjective form. el-sayyara el-oola = the first car. 


aa5er is just like awal. 
aa5er yoam = last day, aa5er el-yoam = the end of the day, aa5er yoam ili / yoami el-a5eer = my last day, el-yoam el-a5eer = the last day.

versions.name: awal / aa5er with el-
versions.one_line: Awal and aa5er + a noun without el- mean first / last, but with el- or a possessive ending they mean the beginning / end of, so for 'my first day' use illi or put the adjective after the noun.
versions.formula: awal / aa5er + noun = first / last; awal / aa5er + el- or ending + noun = beginning / end of
versions.why: English uses 'first' and 'last' the same way everywhere, but in Arabic el- or a possessive ending on the noun turns them into 'the beginning of' and 'the end of', because idafa overrules the other rules.

overlaps.name: awal / oola: before or after the noun
overlaps.why: A13 already covers awal + noun versus awal + el- + noun, and a learner could mix it up with this rule.

payload.what:
For kamaan  to mean also, as well, or too,it doesn’t matter where it’s put in the sentence. 
It matters however, if  we want it to mean, one more or another (meaning more of the same thing)
To mean kamaan  as another of the same thing we put it before the knoun
Kamaan ishi = another / one more thing 
Heyye kamaan bet7eb el-baid / heyye bet7eb el-baid / kamaan heyye bet7eb el-baid = she also likes eggs
payload.label: Change it

payload.what:
It shouldn’t be restricted to nature nouns.
It could be about any noun that sounds feminine, but is masculine or vice versa
Like hand, leg, eye, ear, girl, man, etc.
